headline: Highest risk is medium: shared-output trust and workflow overlap can cascade errors, while prompt injection and leakage are limited by lack of shared channels.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared communication channel is documented between argo-workflows and awesome-nlp, and neither profile shows default ingestion of the other’s outputs. Argo only exposes REST/GRPC APIs and allowlisted egress; awesome-nlp has no I/O surfaces or network egress. Without a bridge, prompt injection is not plausible from the profiles alone.
conditions: IF a manual copy-paste or file bridge is introduced between the agents, injection becomes possible.
IF a shared MCP, queue, or filesystem is added, re-evaluate for instruction hijacking.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Do not pipe one agent’s text directly into the other.
Disable any shared clipboard or message queue.
Review any future connector for provenance tagging.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Argo-workflows touches artifacts and parameters and can make network calls, but awesome-nlp shows no data classes touched and no egress. The pair lacks a documented shared workspace or authenticated principal, so leakage is not evidenced; however, if operators place sensitive artifacts into Argo and then copy outputs into awesome-nlp, small leakage is possible.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same sensitive workspace, leakage risk increases.
IF awesome-nlp is extended to ingest local files or logs, reassess leakage.
mitigations: Keep sensitive artifacts out of shared folders.
Avoid pasting workflow outputs into downstream prompts.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Argo-workflows has API-based orchestration and allowlisted egress, while awesome-nlp exposes no write or network capabilities in the profile. There is no documented overlapping mutable resource or locking conflict, so direct capability contention is limited. Uncertainty remains because awesome-nlp’s write surfaces are unspecified, so the safer low rating is chosen.
conditions: IF awesome-nlp is given filesystem or API write access to the same resource as Argo, conflict risk rises.
IF both agents are granted the same OAuth scope or mutable backend, reassess for contention.
mitigations: Avoid concurrent writes to the same directory or bucket.
Add external locking if a shared backend is introduced.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Argo-workflows can orchestrate downstream actions via APIs, and awesome-nlp is a content/listing-style agent with no verification behavior documented. If Argo consumes awesome-nlp output as authoritative, errors can cascade into workflow actions. Because no explicit validation step is shown, the interaction is plausible in default orchestration patterns, so medium is warranted.
conditions: IF Argo uses awesome-nlp output as an input artifact without validation, cascading errors occur.
IF downstream workflows trigger external actions from that output, impact increases.
mitigations: Log and diff inputs versus acted-on outputs.

E_compliance.rationale: No compliance-sensitive data class, residency mismatch, or retention policy is documented for either argo-workflows or awesome-nlp. Argo touches artifacts and parameters, but the profile does not show PHI, EU PII, or regulated data handling; awesome-nlp lists no data classes. With no compliance-specific pathway evidenced, the risk is none.
conditions: IF regulated data classes are later routed through either agent, compliance must be re-evaluated.
IF residency or retention policies are added to either profile, reassess.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of both agents.
Add retention and residency checks if scope expands.
